sections.h2: Where is Lewiston and what is it known for?
sections.html:
Lewiston is the county seat of Nez Perce County in north central Idaho, at the meeting point of the Snake and Clearwater rivers. The Census Bureau estimates 34,717 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 34,203 at the 2020 census.

It is the principal city of the Lewiston, ID-WA metropolitan area, which includes all of Nez Perce County and Asotin County, Washington. Clarkston, Washington sits immediately west across the state line.

The Port of Lewiston is Idaho's only seaport and the farthest inland port linked to the Pacific Ocean. The Lewiston-Nez Perce County Airport serves the city, and Lewis-Clark State College is a public undergraduate college in town.

sections.h2: What does Lewiston's history and economy mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Lewiston began in the 1861 gold rush era and briefly served as the first capital of Idaho Territory in 1863. A territorial resolution moved the capital to Boise in December 1864.

Today the main industries are agriculture, paper, timber products and light manufacturing. Ammunition manufacturing has a large and growing presence, since Lewiston is the headquarters of ammunition makers CCI and Speer Bullet. The city is also the regional hub for transportation, retail, health care and entertainment, and a base for recreation at the Hells Canyon National Recreation Area.

For a seller, the practical point is that Lewiston is a regional center with its own employers, so most buyers are local or from the surrounding area. Owners who inherit a house or move away for work often need to sell without spending months on repairs and showings.

sections.h2: How do the river valley and the Orchards differ for a house?
sections.html:
Lewiston is split between a low river valley and a high plateau, and the two feel like different markets. Downtown sits between 740 and 780 feet, only slightly above the river, while the terrain climbs quickly away from it. The lowest point in Idaho is on the Snake River in Lewiston, where it meets the Clearwater.

The heavily residential southern half of the city is called the Orchards. It sits at about 1,400 feet and was named for the fruit orchards that once covered it. It was annexed in late 1969, which nearly doubled the city's population and doubled its area. Little sign of orchards remains, though many backyards still hold fruit trees. The Lewiston-Nez Perce County Airport is on the western edge of the Orchards plateau.

  • River and downtown areas: lower elevation, closer to the rivers, older street grid.
  • The Orchards: higher plateau, mostly residential, reached from downtown by the Thain Grade road.

Ask your insurer about flood and drainage exposure if your house is near the river, and note that lenders check flood maps for financed buyers. A cash buyer will still look at the same risks when pricing.

sections.h2: What is the Lewiston climate and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Lewiston has a semi-arid climate with short, mostly mild winters and hot, dry summers. Summer heat is the larger load on roofs, siding and cooling equipment, since snowfall is light.

MeasureLewiston
Average annual precipitation12.31 inches
Average seasonal snowfall10.5 inches
Afternoons at 100 F or higher7.7 per year
Afternoons at 90 F or higher42 per year
Growing season195 days
Record high117 F (July 27, 1939)

The last year Lewiston did not reach 100 degrees was 1995. Tornadoes are very rare, with only three reported in Nez Perce County since 1950. Air conditioning age and attic ventilation are good items to check before you list.

One local event is worth knowing. The city's high reservoir failed on January 18, 2023, releasing roughly three million gallons of water and causing flooding. If your house is in an affected area, keep repair and insurance records handy.

sections.h2: Who handles permits and codes in Lewiston?
sections.html:
The City of Lewiston has adopted current building codes, and permits are required for covered work. The codes are viewable for free on the International Code Council website, and the city publishes a fee schedule and zoning application information.

If you remodeled without a permit, a buyer's inspector may find it. Ask the city before listing. Lewiston Independent School District No. 1 serves the city with seven elementary schools, two junior high schools and two high schools, according to the city's education page, and school assignments are a common buyer question.

Lewiston sits right on the Washington line, next to Clarkston, so some buyers will come from across the river. Idaho law and Nez Perce County offices govern the sale of an Idaho house regardless of where the buyer lives.

sections.h2: How are Nez Perce County property taxes billed and due?
sections.html:
Nez Perce County bills property tax for Lewiston, and the first payment is due December 20. The Idaho State Tax Commission says counties mail bills each November, and owners can pay half by December 20 and the rest by June 20 of the next year.

The county treasurer is at 1230 Main Street, Lewiston, phone 208-799-3030, and online payment is available. The assessor values property at 100% of market value less exemptions as of January 1, with no legal limit on how much a value can change. Each taxing district can raise the property tax part of its budget by no more than 3% unless voters approve more or new construction and annexation add to the base.

The homeowner's exemption covers 50% of the value of a primary home and up to one acre, with a maximum of $125,000, and it ends when ownership changes. The buyer applies for their own. Ask your title company to prorate taxes and to confirm that the first-half payment is current before closing.

sections.h2: What does Idaho law require a Lewiston seller to disclose?
sections.html:
Idaho Code 55-2504 requires sellers of one to four unit residential property to complete a property condition disclosure form, including for nonowner-occupied rentals. It applies to sales, exchanges, installment contracts and options to purchase.

Idaho Code 55-2505 lists exemptions, including court-ordered transfers, transfers by a fiduciary administering an estate, transfers from a decedent's estate, transfers to a lineal relative or spouse, and a transfer by a person who inherited the property and has not occupied it within the past year. Many Lewiston sellers inherited a house, so check these exemptions with an Idaho attorney or title officer.

Even when a form is exempt, you will still be asked about the roof, furnace, water heater, plumbing and any known leaks, because a buyer needs that information to set a price.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Lewiston house usually work?
sections.html:
A cash buyer purchases without a lender, so closing is driven by title work and by the date you choose. You send the address and condition details, review an offer, and a title company clears title and closes.

  • Tell the buyer about occupancy, liens, back taxes and needed repairs.
  • Weigh the offer against listing costs, repair bills and months of carrying costs.
  • Pick a closing date that works with your move or estate timeline.

You owe nothing if you turn an offer down. For some owners a listing nets more, and a local agent can help you compare.

faqs.q: What is the population of Lewiston, Idaho?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 34,717 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 34,203.

faqs.q: When are Nez Perce County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half or full payment is due December 20, and the second half is due June 20 of the following year, under the statewide schedule the Idaho State Tax Commission describes.

faqs.q: Which county office do I contact about my Lewiston property tax bill?
faqs.a: Contact the Nez Perce County Treasurer at 1230 Main Street in Lewiston, phone 208-799-3030. For a value question, start with the county assessor.

faqs.q: What are the Orchards in Lewiston?
faqs.a: The Orchards is the mostly residential southern half of the city on a plateau about 1,400 feet up. It was annexed in late 1969 and is named for the fruit orchards that once covered it.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems when selling a Lewiston house?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Idaho Code 55-2504 requires a property condition disclosure form for one to four unit residential property, with exemptions in 55-2505 such as estate transfers.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lewiston house that has been in my family for years?
faqs.a: Yes. Idaho Code 55-2505 exempts a transfer by someone who inherited the property and has not lived in it within the past year, and transfers by an estate's fiduciary. Confirm your situation with an Idaho attorney or title officer.
